content:
matt: Ran a 30m nsys capture on a mixed-seqlen workload (80% <128, 20% >=2048). Seeing HBM BW spikes and KV cache thrash during long-request tails. Trace: https://perf.redwood/traces/2310456789

sana: Can you paste the nsys command and flags you used?

matt: Sure, exact command:
```
nsys profile --output trace_mixed --trace=cuda,osrt,cublas,cudnn --sample=cpu --capture-range cputrace --force
# workload: replay_mixed.py --workers 12 --seq-dist short:0.8,long:0.2 --microbatch 4
```

kevin: Quick numbers from the trace: HBM read BW baseline ~620 GB/s -> peak ~880 GB/s at long-request bursts; DMA stall cycles up 3.4x; KV cache hitrate falls 98% -> 72% when >2048 seqs; avg tail latency for long requests jumps 4.6x. I exported a small CSV.

tia: My guess: kernel selection path changes for long seqlens (padding -> different gemm kernel), plus microbatching amplifies concurrent KV reads and causes page-level eviction. Do we have kernel-name timeline? nvprof / nsys shows `matmul_v2` switching to `matmul_large_seq` around the spikes.

matt: Yup, timeline shows kernel handoff at t=00:09:12. Perfetto slice: `matmul_large_seq` 1.2ms -> 3.9ms for the same effective FLOPs.

perf-bot: [perf-alert] CI/regression detected on commit abc123: kv-cache hitrate -5% vs baseline, tail-latency +18% :warning:

sana: Can we reproduce with single-host repro? If it's kernel selection + cache pressure we should be able to force a kernel to see effect.

matt: Plan to run experiments:
- (A) Force kernel: REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_fast
- (B) Microbatch=1 (disable coalescing)
- (C) Increase kv_page_bytes=4MB
I'll run (A) now and post traces.

kevin: Also add NVTX ranges around KV read/write to correlate with HBM peaks. And capture `cuptiMetric` counters for DRAM throughput and SM activity.

tia: Small thought: if page-level KV map causes eviction thrash, maybe bias prefetch: when seq>1024, prefetch next 2 pages ahead. Could add heuristic patch.

matt: After forcing kernel -> matmul_fast, HBM peak drops from 880 -> 710 GB/s, long-tail latency reduced ~30%, but KV hitrate still low (78%). So kernel helps but doesn't fully fix cache thrash.

sana: Ok next steps: kevin to run perfetto + cupti sample for a full 1h window, matt to prototype prefetch heuristic in runtime, tia to sketch eviction-aware page sizing. We'll sync in 24h.

kevin: Uploaded perfetto + nsys artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/mixed-seq/2310456789/{perfetto.pb,trace.nsys,summary.csv}

matt: Action items summarized: 1) reproduce baseline + forced-kernel traces (matt) 2) full-capture with NVTX & cupti (kevin) 3) prototype prefetch/eviction tweak (tia) 4) add CI microbench for mixed-seqlen (sana)

sana: thanks. ping me when artifacts uploaded so I can run regression tests.

matt: will do :thumbsup:
